source.title: Keys in the Weights: Transformer Authentication Using Model-Bound Latent Representations
source.authors: Ayse S. Okatan; M. Akbaş; Laxima Niure Kandel; Berker Peköz

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Table II has a labeling ambiguity: its caption describes encoder-attention divergence, while the surrounding text also describes the first reported distance as weight-space distance.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests zero-shot cross-model decoding as a functional measure of representation transferability, rather than measuring representation similarity using the original sources' methods.
record.gate_note: The paper reports cross-decoding results and attention/weight diagnostics. It also discusses prior work on representation similarity and stitching, but those cited results are not recorded here. No learned map, stitching connector, or paired-data alignment procedure is tested.
record.test_reason: The study only swaps decoders zero-shot, with no map of any kind, between same-architecture, different-seed Transformer autoencoders. V4 claims transfer through a simple learned map, stitching layer, relative representation or unsupervised alignment. None of these is tested. V3 says seeds share subspaces but not bases, so identity-swap failure is expected under V3 and V4 alike. The authors' own reading, that the latent is in a random basis from the other model's perspective, fits that. The adapter-learning risk is discussed but not tested. These results show that latents are not interchangeable without an alignment step, a construct no version names. They are recorded under fits_no_version rather than as a challenge to V4.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct, with two additions. The authors say the latent is 'effectively in a random basis' from another model's perspective. They also say the failure reflects incompatible coordinate systems across the whole stack, despite broadly similar first-layer attention. They frame this as a security property and acknowledge that adapter/learned alignment could defeat it, but do not test this. Generalization to larger models and other tasks is left as future work.
record.recipe_differences: Uses zero-shot decoder swapping and decoding metrics, plus attention and distance diagnostics; it does not apply the original sources' representation-similarity methods.
record.method_sensitivity: Decoder match versus different-seed decoder changes the outcome. No systematic sensitivity sweep over metrics, settings, or inputs is reported.

fits_no_version.finding: Three same-architecture, same-data, different-seed Transformer autoencoders on a character identity task each self-decode well (86-92% exact, ~98% token). Feeding one encoder's memory zero-shot into another's decoder gives 0% exact match and ~1% token accuracy (chance ≈1.16%).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Without any alignment map, latents of different-seed models are not directly interchangeable: cross-decoding falls to chance.

fits_no_version.finding: Different-seed models' layer-0 head-averaged encoder attention maps are broadly similar (cosine ~0.90, KL ~0.10, shared diagonal bias), while weight-space ℓ2 distance is ~325.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Different-seed replicas share coarse attention patterns but differ in parameters and fine attention structure.

record.peer_reviewed: Computer Assisted Radiology and Surgery - International Congress and Exhibition
record.problems: The experiments use small Transformer autoencoders on a synthetic character-level identity task, with only three different-seed models. The paper says it evaluates all ordered encoder-decoder pairs but Table I presents only representative pairs, including only M1→M2 and M1→M3 cross-decoding. Evaluation reuses the first 6 test mini-batches. No uncertainty estimates are reported. The study tests zero-shot decoder swapping, not learned cross-model maps or other interoperability procedures. Table II's Dℓ2 label is ambiguous between the surrounding description of weight-space distance and its attention-divergence caption.
record.rows_left_out: No separately reported Table I or Table II numeric entries were omitted. Although the text says all ordered encoder→decoder pairs were evaluated, individual results for unlisted pairs are not stated and were not inferred.

untested.parts: Learned linear/affine maps, stitching layers, relative representations and unpaired alignment between the seed models are all untested. Only zero-shot identity swap is run; adapter alignment is named as a risk but not tried.
No measure of shared features or subspaces across seeds (no CKA/SVCCA, matching or subspace analysis). Only layer-0 head-averaged attention maps and weight distances are reported.
No scale, capability or cross-architecture/objective/data comparison.
No vision-language models or paired data.
No comparison of similarity metrics, settings or inputs.

missing.what: Results for the other ordered cross-decoding pairs (e.g., M2→M1, M2→M3, M3→M1). The text says all pairs were evaluated, but only representative pairs are tabulated.
Decoder self-attention and cross-attention diagnostics, described in Sec. III.F and shown qualitatively, with no numbers given.
missing.locator: Sec. III.F, Sec. IV.C, Sec. V

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T2, challenges V4' is not kept. V4 is about mapping with a simple learned map, and zero-shot identity swap is expected to fail even when V3/V4 hold, because bases differ across seeds. So the 0% results cannot challenge V4. A version or study testing whether a learned linear adapter recovers M1→M2 decoding would be informative, but this paper does not run one. The setting is tiny (d=256, 4 layers, synthetic identity task, 3 seeds, 6 reused test batches, no uncertainty).

versions.untested_parts: No model-size or capability sweep, nor comparison across different architectures, objectives, data, or modalities.
No vision-language models or paired image-caption representations.
The study does not measure shared features or subspaces across seeds. Attention-map diagnostics are not direct tests of shared features or subspaces.
Tests zero-shot decoder swapping only. It does not test learned linear maps, stitching, relative representations, or other alignment procedures.
No recurring interpretable features, neurons, SAE features, or circuits are examined.
No systematic comparison of similarity metrics, settings, inputs, or out-of-distribution data.
The study does not test scaling, plateauing, or whether shared data/objectives versus a common model of reality explain convergence.

reader_labels.condition: Zero-shot decoding of M1 memory with different-seed M2 or M3 decoder
reader_labels.reason: Cross-decoding yields 0.00% exact matches, token accuracy near the stated chance level, and low normalized Levenshtein similarity (r2-r3, r9-r10, r16-r17), unlike self-decoding controls.
